prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key policies and commitments (max 500 words)

Economy, tax and welfare
- Halve employee National Insurance to 6% by April 2027; abolish main rate of self‑employed NI by end of Parliament; no rises in income tax or VAT rates.
- Triple Lock Plus: uprate State Pension and a new age-related personal allowance by the highest of inflation, earnings or 2.5%; maintain pensioner benefits. Target at least £6bn/yr from tackling tax avoidance/evasion.
- Childcare: 30 hours free from nine months to school by Sept 2025; expand wraparound care by Sept 2026. Child Benefit to a household basis, tapering from £120k to £160k.
- Welfare reform: tighter PIP assessments; revised Work Capability Assessment from Sept 2025; move fit notes to specialist assessors; tougher sanctions after 12 months; Fraud Bill giving DWP HMRC‑style powers; complete Universal Credit rollout.

Business, regulation, trade and infrastructure
- Keep corporation tax rate; maintain/extend full expensing (seek to include leasing). SME 10‑point plan (rates relief, VAT smoothing, prompt payments, finance access, female/disabled entrepreneurship).
- R&D: £22bn/yr public spend; maintain R&D tax reliefs; large compute clusters; advanced manufacturing funding (£4.5bn).
- Trade: conclude FTAs with India and GCC; implement CPTPP; maintain TCA without CJEU alignment; NHS excluded from trade talks.
- Planning and delivery: cut major project consent times from ~4 years to 1; streamline EIAs; curb unmeritorious judicial reviews.
- Digital and transport: nationwide gigabit by 2030; standalone 5G to all populated areas; HS2 savings (£36bn) to regional schemes; extend £2 bus fare cap for the whole Parliament; Rail Reform Bill creating Great British Railways; automated vehicles framework.

Energy and net zero
- Annual North Sea oil and gas licensing; new gas power stations for security.
- Treble offshore wind; first two CCS clusters (NW/Teesside–Humber) and progress further (Aberdeenshire/Humber); approve two SMR fleets within 100 days; new gigawatt plant at Wylfa; expand interconnectors.
- Energy bills: maintain price cap; review standing charges; Pumpwatch for fuel prices; local electricity markets; smart tariffs; grid connection reforms.
- Efficiency: £6bn over three years; universal voucher scheme for insulation/solar; nearly half of homes to EPC C+; onshore wind with local consent; prioritise rooftop/brownfield solar; no fracking.
- Import carbon pricing by 2027; manufacturing “bonus” in CfDs for UK supply chains.

Housing and places
- Build 1.6m homes; remove nutrient neutrality barriers with mitigation fees; fast‑track brownfield in 20 largest cities; higher densities in inner London; development corporations (e.g., Leeds, Liverpool, York, Cambridge).
- Infrastructure Levy to fund local services; protect Green Belt.
- First‑time buyers: permanent Stamp Duty threshold £425k; new Help to Buy (up to 20% equity loans); extend Mortgage Guarantee. Two‑year CGT relief for landlords selling to existing tenants.
- Leasehold reform: cap ground rents at £250 then to peppercorn; end misuse of forfeiture; support commonhold.
- Renters Reform: abolish Section 21 after court changes; stronger grounds for anti‑social behaviour evictions; controls on holiday lets; accelerate action on unauthorised traveller sites.
- Towns: £20m endowment each for 105 towns; extend Shared Prosperity and Community Ownership funds; more Freeports/Investment Zones.

Public services: health, policing, education
- NHS: spending to rise above inflation yearly; recruit 92k nurses/28k doctors; expand Pharmacy First; 250 GP surgeries; 50 Community Diagnostic Centres; Dental Recovery Plan (2.5m appointments; NHS service commitment for new dentists; targeted incentives).
- NHS tech: £3.4bn for NHS App “single front door,” AI diagnostics, data/platform upgrades; reduce 5,500 managers; Major Conditions Strategy; Tobacco & Vapes Bill; women’s health and Cass Review implementation; rights to single‑sex accommodation/intimate care.
- Policing/justice: 8,000 neighbourhood officers; facial recognition/tools; Martyn’s Law; hotspot policing, community payback; tougher sentencing (violent/sexual, domestic homicide, knife crime); four new prisons; more foreign national offender removals; anti‑fraud measures (ban SIM farms, cold calls).
- Education/skills: Advanced British Standard (post‑16); 2 hours PE weekly; statutory school mobile‑phone ban; parental access to curriculum materials; register of children not in school; 60,000 SEND places + 15 special free schools; 100,000 extra apprenticeships (funded by closing poor‑outcome degrees); Lifelong Learning Entitlement.
- National Service at 18: either 12‑month full‑time military/cyber or 25 days civic service; Royal Commission; funding rising to £2.5bn in year 5.

Borders, defence and foreign policy
- Migration: binding legal cap on work/family visas that falls annually, subject to annual Parliamentary vote; health checks and higher IHS/insurance; higher visa fees; maintain student dependant limits.
- Illegal migration: monthly Rwanda flights from July; implement Illegal Migration Act; six‑month processing; end hotel use; returns deals; pursue international asylum reform.
- Defence: spend 2.5% of GDP by 2030; at least £10bn for munitions; 5% of defence budget to R&D + 2% exploitation; procurement reform; Veterans Bill and support package.

Environment, farming and fisheries
- Water: unlimited fines; ban bonuses after serious breaches; price‑review reform; river recovery network; extend Southwest £50 rebate.
- Nature: tree planting/peatland funding; urban greening; no deep-sea mining; deposit return scheme; restrict new waste incinerators.
- Farming: increase UK‑wide farming budget by £1bn over the Parliament (inflation‑proofed); legally binding food security target and index; at least 50% public food spend local/higher standards; fast‑track farm infrastructure; five‑year tapered seasonal visas with automation/skills investment.
- Fisheries: replicate £100m UK Seafood Fund; seek expanded quotas in 2026; prioritise inshore fleet in marine planning.

Other
- Backing Drivers Bill: ban road pricing; reverse London ULEZ expansion; local referendums for new LTNs/20mph.
- Equality and law: define “sex” in Equality Act as biological; single legal sex; statutory school guidance for gender‑questioning pupils.
- Culture and sport: maintain grassroots facilities investment; Independent Football Regulator; competitive creative tax incentives; night‑time economy review.
